summary: Contestants act as an office intern for Digital Solutions and use provided materials to produce accurate business documents that meet workplace expectations. All jobs are completed on-site and uploaded electronically. The event tests skills in technology, information management, written communication, professionalism, employability, and office organization.
time_limits: no more than ten (10) minutes orientation
no more than ninety (90) minutes testing time
no more than ten (10) minutes wrap-up
submission_requirements: All contestant-produced jobs completed on-site are uploaded electronically and are not printed at the national level
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Cordless calculator: Electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards. See NLC Calculator Guidelines. Contestants who violate this rule will be disqualified
Suggested resource: ANSI/ARMA 1-1995 - Alphabetic Filing Rules
competencies: Demonstrate proficiency in technology and information management by using industry-standard software to create, edit, organize, and format business documents
Interpret and analyze provided information to determine appropriate document type, structure, and content, ensuring accuracy
Apply effective written communication and professionalism by producing clear, well-formatted documents that follow correct grammar, tone, organizational guidelines, and ethical standards
Exhibit employability and workplace skills, including time management, attention to detail, reliability, safety and responsible use of office tools and equipment
Organize and maintain office inventory and filing systems using digital tools and ARMA standards
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event.
Contestants who have previously competed in Essential Workplace Skills or Advanced Workplace Skills cannot enter this event.

Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification.
